findings.criterion: Workflow usefulness must be evidenced before a pass implies recruiter value
findings.observation: The platform can return a passing local gate without any executed human-workflow review, so the green result proves safety and boundedness but not that an independent recruiter would save time or trust the action.
findings.evidence: plans/2026-08-31-evaluation-first-opik-agent-platform.md:59-65,84-86 require human review to remain separate and ask whether the recruiter completes the loop with less work; evals/v2/scenarios/ts-cap-005.r1.json:52-61, evals/v2/scenarios/ts-act-106.r1.json:52-61, and evals/v2/scenarios/ts-trj-006.r1.json:51-59 all bind human-workflow with requiredForGate=false; apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:228-245 only scores deterministic and outcome evaluators unless optional extras are injected; apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:207-216 and 244-252 call runEvaluationCase without any added evaluators; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:35-56 and 58-75 still report localGateStatus pass.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter owner could read a green evaluation as proof that the loop is operationally better than their manual fallback, even though nobody measured correction burden, useful-next-step quality, or interruption cost on the passing path.
findings.recommendation: Either make workflow evidence required before any release-facing pass claim, or rename the current pass to a narrower safety-only status until adjudicated recruiter workflow results are attached.
findings.verification: After the change, rerunning the same smoke and P0 paths must yield needs_review instead of pass whenever human-workflow evidence is absent, and a passing claim must cite completed workflow adjudications.

findings.criterion: Projected scoring must preserve veto and gate semantics
findings.observation: The local contract keeps gateAuthority and veto separate from quality, but the Opik projection flattens each criterion to 1, 0.5, or 0 and drops those distinctions from the remote score record.
findings.evidence: plans/2026-08-31-evaluation-first-opik-agent-platform.md:62-66 says CI must block regressions without averaging them into a quality score; packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:71-74 says quality values are never averaged into release authority; apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:120-132 and 174 preserve score.gateAuthority and score.veto in the safe envelope; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:84-88 and 289-297 convert statuses to numeric values and only send name, categoryName, value, and reason; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:44-55 shows the remote artifact summarized as remoteFeedbackScoreCount plus remoteLocalGateStatus, not per-score veto semantics.
findings.user_impact: In the remote review surface, a high aggregate can read like a '95' style success score and hide whether the passed points were advisory, blocker-class, or unrelated to recruiter usefulness.
findings.recommendation: Project gateAuthority, veto, and evidence locators into the remote score surface or disable aggregate numeric scoring in reviewer-facing views; any displayed score should be labeled as atomic criterion pass-rate, never candidate quality, business impact, or release approval.
findings.verification: Inspect a projected blocker case and confirm the remote view still exposes blocker-class status and evidence without requiring the local gate artifact to decode a high aggregate.

findings.criterion: Execution output must keep evidence, confirmed state, interpretation, action, and outcome structurally separate
findings.observation: The scenario oracle models those distinctions, but the runner accepts arbitrary executor output, so a remote model or integration can merge proposed and confirmed information into one blob unless a scenario author remembered to write a path-specific check.
findings.evidence: packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:110-156 separates transitions, terminal, proposal, allowedEffects, and forbidden outcomes in the oracle; apps/eval-runner/src/contracts.ts:45-59 defines ModeExecutionObservationV1 with a generic output: JsonValue; apps/eval-runner/src/contracts.ts:482-509 accepts any remote output as long as outcomeStatus, terminalReasonCode, and output exist; packages/evaluation/src/validate.ts:499-585 validates oracle structure but does not validate executor output shape.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter review surface can appear tidy while still hardening interpretation into confirmed state or mixing action with observed outcome, which makes rubber-stamping more likely and weakens auditability when a write is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Require a typed review payload with explicit sections for evidence, confirmed_state, interpretation, proposed_action, and observed_outcome before any evaluator scores the run.
findings.verification: Add a negative test where a remote response collapses proposed and confirmed state into one field; the run should fail contract validation before oracle comparison or projection.

strengths: The repository-level suite is real and validated: pnpm eval:validate passed with 36 scenarios, including 12 p0 cases and explicit dev, held_out, and red_team partitions.

Coverage is strong on the recruiter-controlled safety edge cases the platform names: TS-CAP-005 blocks wrong-speaker attribution, TS-ACT-103 enforces no_action on duplicate reminders, TS-TRJ-006 exercises bounded retry recovery, and TS-ACT-106 exercises permission revocation between preview and execute.
Local gate authority stays local even when projection work fails or deletes: the proof records survived projection failures and verified deletion readback without claiming Opik owns release truth.
missing_evidence: No frozen artifact shows reviewer edit traces or elapsed review time for workflow.correction-burden, so the claim that this loop saves work over the manual fallback is still unproven.
No frozen scenario or proof demonstrates app backgrounding, cross-day return, or resumed review with changed external state preserved for the recruiter.
No frozen artifact shows the exact UI that produced the alleged 95-point interpretation, so I can only assess the transport semantics that would enable that misread.
vetoes: Do not let pass imply recruiter usefulness or field readiness while the same run can pass with zero human-workflow evidence.
Do not surface aggregate remote scores as approval or impact signals while Opik projection drops veto and gate-authority semantics.
open_questions: Is the intended meaning of pass strictly safety-and-integrity, or is product leadership already reading it as recruiter-value proof?
Which surface will reviewers actually use for adjudication: the local artifact with full gate metadata or the Opik trace with flattened numeric scores?
When will workflow.correction-burden be backed by actual reviewer timing and edit evidence rather than only scenario bindings?
